This is the talk page for '''[[Workstation Standard Config]]'''. Use it to
discuss the plugin rows, the disabled rows and the deliberate decisions recorded
on the article page.

== The disabled-rows table reads as a decision list, not a rationale ==

The article lists several rows as "off" but only some carry a real reason. The
<code>skill-badge</code> row says "presentation only", which does not explain why
the row ships disabled in the base bundle rather than being removed. Could the
table get a column that separates '''why the row exists at all''' from '''why it
is off in this deployment'''? That would stop a reader from copying a
deployment-specific override as if it were an upstream decision.

: I agree the two questions are different. The base bundle keeps the row so a UI
  profile can re-enable it; the deployment leaves it off because the workstation
  facade never renders badges. I would support a third column, but let us keep it
  short or the table stops being scannable. ~~~~

== D1 is the only decision with a live health probe ==

D1 records that web search is not provisioned and that the health probe answers
with a missing-service error. The other decisions do not name an observable check
in the same way. If every decision carried the one command that proves its
current state, this page would be much easier to audit after a configuration
change. [[User:Demo-Editor|Demo-Editor]] 09:14, 27 September 2026 (UTC)

: That is a fair request, and the missing-service probe is exactly the pattern to
  copy. One caution: a probe name can drift from the route it calls, so any probe
  added here should quote the raw response instead of paraphrasing it. ~~~~

: A second caution from the same section: the article says re-enabling the
  harness host rows is not sufficient, because the contract is a service, not a
  row. A probe that only checks the row list would give a false green. The right
  probe calls the capability and reads the error code. [[User:Demo-Editor|Demo-Editor]] 09:31, 27 September 2026 (UTC)

== Move the role patch example to its own page? ==

D4 shows a three-row role patch inline. It is useful, but it is really a worker
setup recipe rather than a workstation standard-config fact. Should it move to a
page of its own, and leave D4 as a short pointer? ~~~~

: I would keep a one-line summary and move the full patch. The patch is the part
  most likely to be copied, and it is the part most likely to go stale. ~~~~
